bib.title: LongICLBench: Long-context LLMs Struggle with Long In-context Learning

question: Can long-context LLMs comprehend an entire long input, tested via in-context learning on extreme-label classification tasks of increasing label-space size and length?
hypothesis: Initial hypothesis: the strongest LLMs like GPT-4-turbo are capped at a certain complexity level between DialogRE and Discovery.
contributions: Identify ICL on extreme-label classification as a testbed for long-context ability and build LongICLBench.
Evaluate recent long-context LLMs at gradually increasing difficulty and find sensitivity to instance position in the prompt.

method.summary: Six extreme-label classification datasets (28 to 174 classes, 2K-50K tokens) are turned into few-shot prompts of 1-5 rounds (one example per label per round). 15 long-context LLMs (11 open ~7B, 4 API) are evaluated on 500 test examples per dataset. A TacRED pilot compares scattered vs grouped demonstration order.

prompts.text: Given a comment, please predict the emotion category of this comment. The prediction answer must come from the demonstration examples with the exact format. The examples are as follows: {comment: "...comment..." emotion category: "...emotion..."} x repeat n times

Given a customer service query, please predict the intent of the query. The predicted answer must come from the demonstration examples with the exact format. The examples are as follows: {service query: "...service..." intent category: "...intent..."} x repeat n times

Given a sentence and a pair of subject and object entities within the sentence, please predict the relation between the given entities. The examples are as follows: {sentence: "...sentence... the subject is "...subject..." the object is "...object..." the relation between the two entities is: "...relation..."} x repeat n times

Given the sentence, please find the name entities in the sentence and their corresponding entity types in the strict format of the given examples as following (Entity: EntityType): {"...entity...": "...entity type..."} x repeat n times

Given the dialogue, please find the name pair entities in the dialogue and their corresponding relation types in the strict format of given examples as following (note that the number of entities has to strictly have the same value as the number of respective relation): {Dialogue: "...dialogue..." The list of entity pairs are "..." The "...number of pairs..." respective relations between each entity pair are: "..."} x repeat n times

Given two sentence1 and sentence2, please predict the conjunction word between the two sentences. The predicted answer must come from the demonstration examples with the exact format. The examples are as follows: {"...sentence1..." ( ) "...sentence2..." the conjunction word in ( ) is "...conjunction..."} x repeat n times

results.claim: Gemini-1.5-Pro is the only model clearly above zero on Discovery (174 labels), at 14% accuracy with 1 round (10K tokens); it falls to 6.0, 3.2, 1.8, 2.8 at 20K-50K.
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; Discovery

results.claim: Abstract/intro: on Discovery all LLMs get close to zero except Gemini-1.5-Pro with 14% accuracy.
results.quote: all LLMs achieve close-to-zero performance except Gemini-1.5-Pro with 14% accuracy

results.claim: A fine-tuned BERT model reaches 87% on Discovery, versus near zero for in-context LLMs.
results.setup: Discovery; fine-tuned BERT (Table 6 lists SoTA MTL 87.4)
results.quote: In contrast, a fine-tuned BERT model (Kenton & Toutanova, 2019) can achieve 87%.
results.note: Table 6 labels the 87.4 row 'SoTA (MTL)', the intro attributes 87% to fine-tuned BERT.

results.claim: GPT4-turbo scores 1.5 at 1 round on Discovery then 0.5 for 2-5 rounds; GPT4o 2.8 then 0.8, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4; Claude3-Opus 1.2 then 0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.2; all open-source models are 0 (ChatGLM3 1.0 at 2R, RWKV 0.2 at 2R).
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; Discovery

results.claim: Claude3-Opus on DialogRE collapses with context: 16.8 (8K), 30.3 (13K), 15.3 (19K), 0.8 (25K), 0 (32K).
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; DialogRE

results.claim: GPT4-turbo on DialogRE rises monotonically: 42.9, 47.8, 52.0, 55.9, 57.7 from 8K to 32K; SoTA HiDialog 77.1.
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; DialogRE

results.claim: Claude3-Opus on BANKING77 degrades with more demos: 60.0, 62.6, 62.2, 43.8, 26.0 (2K to 14K).
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; BANKING77

results.claim: LLaMA-2-7B-LongLora scores 0 at every length (1R-5R) on BANKING77, and also on TacRED, DialogRE, Discovery, GoEmotions and Few-NERD.
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; BANKING77

results.claim: On BANKING77 GPT4-turbo reaches 84.4 at 5R (14K) vs SoTA RoBERTa+ICDA 94.4.
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds

results.claim: Grouping same-label demos on TacRED (3 rounds, 10K tokens) drops GPT4-turbo from 79.5 to 59.2.
results.setup: TacRED, 3 rounds, 41 labels x3 = 123 demos, scattered vs grouped
results.quote: experiencing a notable decline in performance by 20.3% and 22.3%
results.table: Table 10, row GPT4-turbo, columns Scatter 79.5, Grouped 59.2, delta -20.3

results.claim: Grouping on TacRED drops Gemini-1.5-Pro from 79.6 to 57.3.
Grouping on TacRED drops Mistral-7B-v0.2-base from 51.6 to 5.1.
results.note: Text says Mistral and InternLM2 show significant drops. InternLM2 15.5 to 4.8 (-9.7); Qwen 45.2 to 33.0 (-12.2); ChatGLM3 38.9 to 35.6 (-3.3).

results.claim: Models with different mechanisms do not all benefit from more demos; on TacRED and DialogRE only GPT4-turbo and GPT4o consistently benefit and others peak mid-context (13K-25K).
results.quote: only GPT4-turbo and GPT4o can consistently benefit from more demonstrations, all of the other models reach their peak at the middle with context length around 13K to 25K
results.note: Table 4 shows Gemini-1.5-Pro also rising roughly (72.6 to 82.3), so the text claim is not fully matched by the table.

results.claim: Transformer-based models beat RNN-like (RWKV, Mamba); Mamba-2.8B scores 0 on all datasets, RWKV near 0 on most.
results.quote: models of Transformer-based architecture perform consistently better than the RNN-based ones in all the evaluated datasets

results.claim: Mistral-7B-v0.2-base on TacRED declines from 53.3 (4K) to 42.3 (18K), and on DialogRE from 24.0 to 21.1: more demos hurt.
results.setup: 500 test examples per dataset, even label distribution, base models (API models as served), demonstrations of 1 to 5 rounds; TacRED

results.claim: Authors' hypothesis: even strongest LLMs like GPT-4-turbo are capped at a complexity level between DialogRE and Discovery.
results.quote: Our initial hypothesis suggests that the strongest LLMs like GPT-4-turbo are capped at a certain complexity level between DialogRE and Discovery.

limits: Authors: LongICLBench covers only one evaluation type, extreme-label classification via long ICL.
Decoding settings, temperature, seeds and max tokens are not stated; single run per cell, no variance.
Open-source models are base (not instruction-tuned) 7B, so near-zero scores may reflect format-following failure rather than long-context comprehension; failed runs marked with a cross in Table 6.
The grouped/scattered analysis is a pilot on one dataset (TacRED, 3 rounds) with 123 demos.
API models (GPT-4-turbo, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini-1.5-Pro) are versions of early 2024 and have dated.
Table 2 lists RWKV-5-World as 3B but Tables 3-8 list 7B.
